sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Augusta?
sections.html:
The Richmond County Tax Commissioner bills and collects, and the Richmond County Board of Assessors sets the value. Augusta and Richmond County merged into one consolidated government on July 1, 1996, so county offices serve the whole city, though the separate towns of Blythe and Hephzibah stayed outside the merger and have their own tax districts.

The Tax Commissioner works from the Municipal Building at 535 Telfair Street, Suite 100, Augusta, GA 30901, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 1427, Augusta, GA 30903. The main line is 706-821-2391. The Board of Assessors answers value and appeal questions at 706-821-2310, and owners can look up their record and file an appeal online at augustarichmondtaxassessor.com.

  • Payments are accepted online, by mail, by phone at (706) 252-9080, in person at the Municipal Building, or at the South and West Augusta tag offices by debit card, credit card or check.
  • Every office has a drop box outside.
  • If a lender escrows your tax, the owner is still the one responsible for confirming payment.

Bills here go out near the end of September and fall due November 30. Pay inside the first 20 days and you take 1 percent off the tax portion, a perk few Georgia counties offer.

After the due date, interest is added every month and a one-time 10 percent penalty is added in late December. Ask the office on 706-821-2391 for the exact monthly interest figure before paying a delinquent bill. Partial payments are accepted once bills are mailed, and penalties and interest continue on whatever remains.

An account with an outstanding balance is subject to a lien. Before a lien, known as a Fi.Fa., is issued, the office sends a 30-day notice of intent. Fi.Fa.s are recorded on the General Execution Docket of the Clerk of Superior Court, stay in effect for seven years, and may show up on credit reports. Paying the taxes, fees, penalties and interest cancels it.

Your rate turns on which of four tax districts holds the house. A mill is $1 of tax for every $1,000 of assessed value, and the tax is the assessed value, less exemptions, multiplied by the millage rate.

Two bodies set the rates that make up the total: the Richmond County Board of Commissioners and the Richmond County Board of Education. The tax commissioner's office only bills and collects.

Voters approved a Floating Local Option Sales Tax (FLOST) on May 19, 2026. It is a 0.5 percent sales tax collected in Richmond County starting October 1, 2026, authorized for five years, and its proceeds must be used to reduce property taxes. Rollbacks show up on tax bills a year later, starting in 2027, and apply to a portion of the general county maintenance and operations levy.

Augusta is Georgia's third-largest city, with an estimated 201,999 residents, and faces North Augusta, South Carolina, across the Savannah River. It covers more than 300 square miles, so density is low.

Prices run far below Atlanta's. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $178,400, half of the 75,222 households own (50.8 percent), and the typical monthly rent is $1,142. Median household income is $55,485. Fort Gordon, Augusta University and the Savannah River Site are the largest employers, which means military and medical moves drive a lot of the buying and selling.

You have 45 days from the date on the assessment notice to appeal, and the same window works for a homestead application if you missed the earlier filing date. Notices usually mail in late June.

The notice is not a tax bill. It shows the assessed value, exemptions, and the right to appeal, and under Georgia Senate Bill 566 it now includes an Estimated Tax Savings section in place of the old estimated tax tables. Appeals can be filed online through the Property Search tool at augustarichmondtaxassessor.com, or by mail, email or in person. Augusta also has a local floating homestead exemption that limits certain increases in assessed value on qualifying primary residences.

Homestead applications go to the Tax Commissioner, which forwards them to the Board of Assessors for the final decision. A denial can be appealed to the Board of Equalization. An exemption renews automatically, and you do not have to apply again unless the ownership, name or deed changes. Refinancing does not affect it, and all vehicles owned by the applicant and spouse must be registered in Richmond County. When mailing an application, use certified mail, because metered postage dates are not accepted as timely.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax when you sell
sections.html:
Whoever owned the house on January 1 is billed for the year, though the purchase agreement can shift that cost to the buyer at closing. Your closing attorney sorts out the split.

A sale in, say, July still sends the bill to the earlier owner. Behind on payments? The office refreshes balances every night, so ask for the current figure and put the bill number or map and parcel number on any written request. A property can also show as under appeal or pending an assessment change order, in which case the bill may not yet be due, so confirm the status before paying.

If delinquent taxes lead to a tax sale, the county holds the auction on the first Tuesday of the month in the Commission Chambers of the Municipal Building at 535 Telfair Street, and it advertises the sale in the Augusta Chronicle for four consecutive weeks first. Selling first lets the closing pay the county out of your proceeds.

sections.h2: Before you list an Augusta house
sections.html:
Look up your parcel at augustarichmondtaxassessor.com and write down the tax district, because that district fixes the rate your buyer will pay. Then phone 706-821-2391 for the balance and make sure the Clerk of Superior Court shows no Fi.Fa. against the parcel. Tell buyers that a homestead exemption is theirs to file for.

Give the closing attorney the balance, the bill number and any open appeal status so the settlement statement is right. A cash buyer can close quickly, but a lien or unpaid balance still has to clear at the table.

faqs.q: What is the due date for Augusta property tax?
faqs.a: November 30. Owners who pay within the first 20 days get a 1 percent discount on the tax portion. After the due date, monthly interest applies and a one-time 10 percent penalty follows in late December.

faqs.q: Is Augusta's property tax rate the same everywhere in Richmond County?
faqs.a: No. The county lists four tax districts for 2026: Urban at 28.284, County with fire at 26.28, Hephzibah at 24.939 and Blythe with fire at 26.839. The district printed on your bill decides the rate.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal an Augusta assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date on the assessment notice. Once that window closes, the right to appeal that year's value ends, and the next chance comes with the following year's notice.

faqs.q: What does FLOST do for Augusta homeowners?
faqs.a: FLOST is a 0.5 percent sales tax that began October 1, 2026, with proceeds used to cut property taxes. Rollbacks appear on tax bills starting in 2027, as a reduction to a portion of the county's general operating levy.

faqs.q: Who do I call about an Augusta property value?
faqs.a: Call the Richmond County Board of Assessors at 706-821-2310. For billing, payments or homestead questions, call the Tax Commissioner's office at 706-821-2391.
